read_this_first.summary: Every number in this file was regenerated or extracted from a committed artifact on this machine. Nothing is simulated-for-illustration and nothing is hand-tuned. The model has SYNTHETIC anatomy and a SYNTHETIC lead field, its amortised posterior does not recover its own parameters, and it has no validated held-out performance. All five claim gates G1-G5 are COULD_NOT_RUN. These demos show machinery working; none of them is evidence about brains.

demos.demo1: ran - trained checkpoint, forward multirate rollout
demos.demo2: regenerated - dynamics module, no trained checkpoint involved
demos.demo3: ran - field physics, no trained checkpoint involved

corrections_to_the_brief.claim: EEG at its native millisecond rate
corrections_to_the_brief.finding: The model has exactly TWO clocks: fast (dt_model=0.008 s, 125 Hz) and slow (dt_model*hemo_ratio=0.2 s, 5 Hz). The EEG head is a memoryless per-timestep map over the state and therefore emits at 125 Hz. There is no millisecond EEG clock in scwbd.foundation. The demonstrated contrast is 125 Hz vs 5 Hz.

corrections_to_the_brief.claim: 80.2% of parameter mass in the _orig_mod keys
corrections_to_the_brief.finding: Correct against TRAINABLE parameters (1,410,297 / 1,757,613 = 80.24%). Against all state-dict tensor elements (6,733,924, including the anatomy-derived coupling buffers) the same 29 keys are 20.94%. Both denominators are recorded.

corrections_to_the_brief.claim: delay RMSE native-clock 0.376 ms vs naive-resampling 5.000 ms
corrections_to_the_brief.finding: 0.376 ms does not appear anywhere in reports/identifiability/. The 5.000 ms figure is real: it is joint_resampled in the weak_coupling_long_delay regime, where joint_native scores 1.2346 ms (not 0.376). The per-regime table is reported instead of a single pair, and the preregistered criterion C2_native_beats_resampled is recorded as FAILED in the artifact.

Reproduced exactly as max||E|| = 134.5164 V/m. Note that PhysicalDose.peak() returns the largest single Cartesian COMPONENT, 106.7257 V/m - a different quantity. The test that pins this reads dose.peak() but its comment records the max-norm value.

Reproduced exactly on CUDA. But the source test's own docstring states the peak LOCATION is not a claim: the supracritical curve is a flat plateau whose argmax moves to G=4.0 on CPU from the same seed. What is asserted is onset at the transition and degradation under over-coupling.

demo1_multirate_forward_run.title: Multirate whole-brain forward run: one latent trajectory, two instruments, two native clocks
demo1_multirate_forward_run.what_it_is: A free-running (autoregressive, no teacher forcing) rollout of the trained SC-WBD-001-beta operator over 454 regions. The regional activity, the EEG channels and the BOLD signal are all read off the SAME state tensor: EEG through the lead-field head on the fast clock, BOLD through the Balloon-Windkessel head on the slow clock. Nothing is resampled.
demo1_multirate_forward_run.clock_correction: The model has exactly TWO clocks, not three. The EEG head is a memoryless per-timestep map over the state, so it emits at the FAST clock (8 ms, 125 Hz) - there is no millisecond-rate EEG clock in scwbd.foundation. BOLD is stepped every 25th fast step (200 ms, 5 Hz). The multirate claim demonstrated here is 125 Hz vs 5 Hz off one trajectory, not 1 kHz vs 5 Hz.

spectral.note: Honest characterisation of what the free-running trajectory actually looks like. It is dominated by slow, largely non-oscillatory drift; it does not exhibit a physiological EEG spectrum, and no claim that it should is made.

neural_activity_carpet.note: all 454 regions x 100 frames; decimation is for FILE SIZE, the model ran at 125 Hz

neural_activity_logvar_mean.note: per-region time-mean of the heteroscedastic predictive log-variance

eeg_traces.units: arbitrary (lead field is analytic single-sphere; physical_scale_volts_per_unit recorded in provenance)

bold_traces.units: fractional BOLD signal change (Buxton output equation, v0=0.04)

psd_activity_mean_over_regions.units: power (arbitrary), Hann-windowed periodogram averaged over 454 regions

psd_eeg_mean_over_channels.units: power (arbitrary), Hann-windowed periodogram averaged over 64 channels

checkpoint_load_trap.description: 29 of the 85 model keys carry torch.compile's `_orig_mod.` infix because the trainer compiles `local` and `residual` only on CUDA. A strict=False load against an uncompiled module drops all 29 and leaves those submodules at random initialisation while reporting success.
checkpoint_load_trap.note_on_the_80_2_percent_figure: 80.2% is correct against TRAINABLE parameters (1,410,297 of 1,757,613 in the checkpoint's own parameter_report). Against all state-dict tensor elements (6,733,924, which include the anatomy-derived coupling buffers) the same 29 keys are 20.94%. Both denominators are reported so neither figure misleads.

demo2_criticality.title: Criticality: FC-SC correlation onsets at the bifurcation of global coupling G
demo2_criticality.what_it_is: Reduced Wong-Wang mean-field on a 40-region SYNTHETIC distance-dependent connectome. FC is computed on simulated BOLD through Balloon-Windkessel (TR 0.2 s), not on the raw gating variable. Reproduces the mechanism behind Deco et al. 2013 (J Neurosci 33:11239); it is NOT a fit to measured FC.
demo2_criticality.model_used: scwbd.dynamics.ReducedWongWangSingle - NOT the trained SC-WBD-001-beta checkpoint

fc_sc_correlation.units: Pearson r between off-diagonal simulated FC and synthetic SC

fc_mean.role: control - rules out 'more coupling = more correlation'

dS_dG.note: finite difference; G_c is the RIGHT endpoint of the steepest interval

demo2_criticality.caveat_from_the_test_itself: The location of the FC-SC peak is NOT a claim. The supracritical curve is a flat plateau and its argmax is not stable across floating-point backends: the test docstring records ~0.21-0.25 on CUDA and ~0.24-0.29 on CPU for G in [0.8, 3.0], with argmax landing on G=2.0 on CUDA and G=4.0 on CPU from the same seed. What is asserted is that structure APPEARS at the transition and is LOST under over-coupling. Also: the synthetic connectome W is drawn on-device, so CPU and CUDA runs generate DIFFERENT connectomes and therefore different fc_sc values.

demo3_tms_efield.title: TMS induced E-field on a cortical surface, figure-eight coil at a realistic pose
demo3_tms_efield.what_it_is: Quasi-static induced E-field from a 70 mm figure-eight coil, biphasic pulse, 4 mm standoff, evaluated on a 2562-vertex cortical shell of a layered spherical head. Field physics only - no neural response, no target engagement.

geometry.anatomy_note: This is an ANALYTIC SPHERE, not a head. run_field_gates.GEOMETRY_PROVENANCE records uses_subject_anatomy=False and uses_scwbd_anatomy_load_anatomy=False. The repo does own real cortical surfaces (scwbd/anatomy/geometry.py) but they are not wired to the field solver.

demo3_tms_efield.peak_definition_note: TWO DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. `peak_magnitude_V_per_m` is max||E|| over vertices = 134.5164 V/m, which is the ~134.5 V/m figure in circulation. `PhysicalDose.peak()` is `value.abs().max()`, the largest single CARTESIAN COMPONENT = 106.7257 V/m. The assertion in tests/intervene/test_tms_efield.py:350 reads dose.peak() but its comment records the max-norm value; both are reported here so the difference is not silently inherited.

efield_magnitude_V_per_m.note: one value per cortical-shell vertex, same order as vertex_positions_m

vertex_positions_m.units: m (head frame, origin at head centre)

N6_standoff.claim_text: The magnetically induced E-field solver reproduces the closed-form (Sarvas / Heller-van Hulsteyn) solution for a spherically symmetric conductor, validated independently of any neural-response model.
N6_standoff.note: validates the charge-BEM solver against an independently derived spectral reference, STANDOFF geometry only

N8_contact.claim_text: The induced-field solver is validated in the CONTACT regime (a coil element at clinical standoff from the scalp, a/R_c >= 0.95) to a preregistered tolerance — the geometry the downstream targeting consumer actually uses.
N8_contact.note: near-contact geometry, graded mesh; validated against AxialInductionReference

demo4_identifiability.title: Identifiability: theta-profile information and delay recovery by design
demo4_identifiability.what_it_is: Fisher/profile-likelihood identifiability benchmark on a 3-region synthetic generator, comparing observation designs. Extracted verbatim from a committed artifact; nothing here was recomputed for the demo.

theta_profile_min_eigenvalue_nonprior.units: dimensionless (min eigenvalue of the likelihood-only profile information for the preregistered theta subset)

low_snr_short_delay.note: discriminating: true delay is placed away from the prior mean

reference.note: DEGENERATE: the true delay equals the prior mean, so a design that learns nothing about the delay scores a perfect delay error. Not discriminating.

weak_coupling_long_delay.note: discriminating: true delay is placed away from the prior mean

verdict_as_recorded.consequence: Criteria ['C1_fusion_information', 'C2_native_beats_resampled', 'C3_intervention_information'] were fully evaluated and FAILED; criteria ['C4_calibrated_recovery', 'C5_recovery_improvement'] could not be evaluated in every regime and are reported as NOT EVALUATED rather than as failures. On the evidence that was evaluable, the claim that cross-method integration resolves these dynamics must be narrowed; the compiler may still be useful as a provenance system (thesis_contract.tex sec. 0.3).
